grain.source: USDA 20004 barley hulled 354, 20072 wheat hard red winter 327, 20038 oats 389; edible 0.92 (oat and barley husk)
grain.note: boiled whole: the ladder's bottom rung (D2-60)

beans.unit: 1 kg dried shelled beans or peas
beans.source: USDA 16052 broad beans mature 341; 16085 split peas 341
beans.note: boiled: the same rung as whole grain; D2-53 'less food' kept or not (part 3)

meal.unit: the meal of 1 kg grain (hand-ground, unsifted)

flour.unit: the flour of 1 kg grain (mill, lightly sifted)
flour.note: porridge or bread: the middle rung

bread.unit: the bread of 1 kg flour (about 1.4 kg of loaves)
bread.source: USDA 18075 whole-wheat bread 252; 1 kg flour bakes about 1.4 kg
bread.note: the top rung: the grain's whole energy (no gain past it)

green grain.unit: 1 kg of green ears and straw

green beans.source: USDA 11052 snap beans 31; broad beans immature 11088 72

meat.unit: 1,500 kcal of edible meat (about 1 kg: 1.25 kg venison, 0.6 kg fat beef)
meat.source: USDA 17164 deer 120, 17165 wild boar 122, 13000s beef composite 200-290, 17178 rabbit wild 114
meat.note: cooked; raw 0.53 of cooked kept as a design factor (fire matters)

dried meat.unit: half the weight of the meat that made it

smoked meat.unit: half the weight of the meat that made it

salt meat.unit: meat salted in a tub, the same weight

fish.unit: 1,150 kcal of edible fish (about 1 kg gutted and headed river fish)
fish.source: USDA 15xxx trout rainbow wild 119, pike 88, perch 91, carp 127, eel 15025 184, Atlantic salmon wild 15076 142

milk.source: USDA 01077 whole milk 61; medieval milk fatter (Trow-Smith)

cheese.unit: 1 kg hard cheese (from about 10 kg milk)
cheese.source: USDA 01009 cheddar 403; skim-milk hard cheese about 330
cheese.note: the engine's 6 milk to a cheese becomes 10 (part 2)

egg.unit: 1 kg eggs in shell (about 20 medieval eggs)
egg.note: the engine's egg unit is on the old compressed clock (part 2)

roots.source: est: no table; comparable roots USDA 11298 parsnip 75, 11104 burdock 72

mushrooms.source: USDA 11239 chanterelle 32 (38 in some releases), 11260 white mushroom 22

samphire.source: est: no USDA row; about 20 to 25 kcal (glasswort composition)

hedge fruit.unit: 1 kg crab apples, sloes, haws, hips
hedge fruit.source: USDA 09003 apple 52 (crab 76), 09136 rose hips 162; stones and cores 0.3

hazel nuts.source: USDA 12120 hazelnuts 628; kernel 0.40 to 0.45 of the nut in shell

acorns.source: USDA 12058 acorns raw 387; bitter until leached
acorns.note: raw acorns kept almost inedible (tannin): a physical fact, stated as a factor

acorn meal.unit: the leached meal of 1.5 kg acorns (3 acorns make 2)

tallow.note: kept inedible on purpose: it is the lights' good (brief 3 §5); real fat is the densest food there is

offal.unit: what is left of a carcass

red deer.note: engine mass 90 (a hind to a woodland stag); larder weight about 0.7 of live, carcass 0.55 to 0.6

wild boar.source: USDA 17165 wild boar 122 lean; autumn fat raises it

wildfowl.source: USDA 05141 duck wild meat 123, with skin 211

salmon.source: USDA 15076 Atlantic salmon wild 142; FAO-fish edible 0.6 to 0.65

lamprey.source: est (lampreys are fatty; no USDA row)

cow.source: Albarella (size); beef carcass yields; USDA beef composite

farming, plough-broken.source: Titow; Clark; Henley (an acre a day a team)

milking (3 cows a unit).note: milking alone, not the herd's keep

gathering, autumn.source: Holst (hazel); Kelly (nuts, acorns 1,000 to 1,500 with leaching)

sources.USDA: USDA ARS, FoodData Central, SR Legacy (2019): energy a 100 g edible portion, raw unless stated; NDB number given
sources.MW: McCance and Widdowson's The Composition of Foods, 7th summary ed. (PHE/RSC 2015; CoFID 2021): edible portions
sources.FAO-fish: FAO Fisheries Technical Paper 309 (1989), Yield and nutritional value of the commercially more important fish species
sources.FAO-WHO: FAO/WHO/UNU, Human energy requirements, FAO Food and Nutrition Technical Report 1 (2004)
sources.Compendium: Ainsworth et al., 2011 Compendium of Physical Activities (METs for farming, hand tools, hunting, fishing)
sources.Titow: J. Z. Titow, Winchester Yields (1972): seed ratios and yields an acre on the bishop's estates, 1209 to 1349
sources.Campbell: B. M. S. Campbell, English Seigniorial Agriculture 1250-1450 (2000): yields, seeding rates, crop mixes
sources.Clark: G. Clark, 'Labour productivity in English agriculture, 1300-1860', in Campbell and Overton (eds), Land, Labour and Livestock (1991): days an acre by task
sources.Henley: Walter of Henley's Husbandry and the Seneschaucy (c. 1280; ed. Oschinsky 1971): a plough's acre a day; dairy yields
sources.Langdon: J. Langdon, Horses, Oxen and Technological Innovation (1986): plough teams and their work
sources.Kelly: R. L. Kelly, The Lifeways of Hunter-Gatherers (2nd ed. 2013), ch. 3, return rates by resource (post-encounter, kcal an hour)
sources.Simms: S. R. Simms, Behavioral Ecology and Hunter-Gatherer Foraging (BAR S381, 1987): Great Basin return rates
sources.Hill: Hill, Kaplan, Hawkes and Hurtado, 'Foraging decisions among Ache hunter-gatherers', Ethology and Sociobiology 8 (1987)
sources.Holst: D. Holst, 'Hazelnut economy of early Holocene hunter-gatherers', Journal of Archaeological Science 37 (2010)
sources.Mitchell: Mitchell, Staines and Welch, Ecology of Red Deer (1977); BDS larder weights; carcass yields of red and roe deer
sources.Albarella: U. Albarella, 'Size, power, wool and veal: zooarchaeological evidence for late medieval innovations' (1997); medieval cattle withers heights, so live weights of about 250 to 350 kg
sources.Trow-Smith: R. Trow-Smith, A History of British Livestock Husbandry to 1700 (1957): medieval milk yields
sources.Poole: Poole et al., 'Long-term variation in numbers and biomass of silver eels being produced in two European river systems', ICES J. Mar. Sci. 75 (2018): Burrishoole over 4,000 silver eels a year before 1982, about 2,000 after; 1.1 to 1.2 kg/ha a year
sources.Tesch: F.-W. Tesch, The Eel (5th ed. 2003): silver eel sizes (males about 0.1 kg, females 0.3 to 1.5 kg)
sources.WGEEL: ICES WGEEL reports: glass eel recruitment since 1980 at a few to ten per cent of 1960-79 levels
sources.Darby: H. C. Darby, The Domesday Geography of Eastern England (1952, 1971): eel renders in sticks of 25; mills and fisheries rendering hundreds to thousands of eels a year
sources.Bush: River Bush salmon station (AFBI, Northern Ireland; Hansard written answers 1990-95): wild smolts 17,000 to 23,000 a year (1987-91), sea catch of Bush fish about 4,800 to 5,900 (1987-89); catchment about 340 km2 (recalled)
sources.quern: ethnographic and experimental quern rates: about 1 to 2 kg of grain an hour by rotary quern (estimate from the experimental literature; check)
sources.est: estimate (no table gives it): the reasoning is in the note

eel.src: Poole (Burrishoole about 2,000 to 4,000+ a year from about 90 km2: 22 to 45); WGEEL (pre-1980 recruitment several times today's)

salmon.src: Bush (about 20,000 smolts and 5,000+ adults taken at sea from about 340 km2)
